prompt: Bond dissociation energies (BDE): for toluene (PhCH₃), the benzylic C–H BDE is ~90 kcal/mol vs ~104 kcal/mol for methane. The difference reflects:

options.label: Resonance stabilization of the benzyl radical by the π system of the ring (~14 kcal/mol).
A weaker σ C–H bond in toluene.
Polarity of the C–H bond in toluene.

explanation: BDE measures the energy to form R• + H•. Lower BDE at benzylic C–H means the resulting radical is more stable — the ring's π system delocalizes the unpaired electron over four positions.
